title: The manifest is environment-aware; the exact environment shape is elicited from the operator, not assumed
description: Each manifest entry carries per-environment metadata: at minimum a path or reference the vendor resolves per environment, and optionally per-environment rotation and required-or-optional overrides. The set of environment names (for example `dev`, `ci`, `live`; or `dev`, `staging`, `prod`; or a project-specific list) is elicited from the operator at first apply, recorded in the manifest header, and enforced from then on. The Secrets Manager client resolves against exactly one environment per process, selected by an unambiguous boot input (a process-scoped variable or a boot flag), and a missing per-environment resolution for the active environment fails boot for a required secret and is served as null for an optional one.
rationale: Every project has a slightly different environment shape and forcing one on them is how the manifest becomes the thing developers work around instead of with. Eliciting the shape at apply time (and freezing it in the manifest header) keeps the manifest legible to a first-time reader and keeps the boot-time selection unambiguous.
